title: Development of novel approaches for gene editing therapies of cystic fibrosis
text:
This proposal will use rAAV-delivered and CRISPR-mediated gene editing in airway progenitor cells to
permanently correct the defects in CFTR gene in cystic fibrosis patients. In addition, it will develop the next
generation rAAV vector aligned with the gene editing approach in airway progenitor cells.

title: Forward Genetic Analysis of Cortical Circuits and Structure
text:
Birth defects affecting the structure of the mammalian nervous system are fairly common (~15/10,000 births).
While these congenital defects have a genetic component, the precise genes responsible are still largely
unknown. This proposal will use genetic approaches with emerging sequencing and animal transgenic
technologies to study the etiology of defects in cortical development with an additional focus on circuit
formation and function and lead to more effective clinical genetics, diagnostics, and therapeutic interventions.

title: Regulation of cell growth and proliferation by the Hippo pathway
text:
Precise regulation of cell growth and proliferation is necessary to maintain tissue homeostasis and organ size,
and this regulation is predominantly controlled by two highly conserved signaling pathways: the Hippo and
mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) pathways. The goal of this proposal is to identify and mechanistically
define proteins that coordinate the activities of these two pathways. Successful completion of these aims will
provide new insights into how these pathways are deregulated in human disease.

title: Metabolic and molecular regulation of myeloid cell functions in brain cancer
text:
Glioblastoma is an incurable primary malignant brain cancer and is characterized by a profound
immunosuppressive microenvironment which renders this cancer highly resistant to immunotherapy. The
proposed studies will exert a profound effect in the field by dissecting targetable metabolic and molecular
mechanisms regulating the function of tumor associated macrophages, which are instrumental for the
maintenance of immunosuppressive state of glioblastoma. This mechanistic understanding will be critical to
provide our clinical partners with novel therapeutic approaches to overcome immunosuppression and to enhance
the efficacy of immunotherapy in GBM patients, which will be tested in subsequent clinical trials.

title: A nanofiber-hydrogel composite plug for perianal fistula repair
text:
There are no effective treatments for perianal fistula (PAF), which occurs in up to 40% of Crohn’s disease pa-
tients. This proposed study aims to develop a biostimulatory nanofiber-hydrogel composite plug to promote
tissue healing and test its efficacy to repair PAF in rodent and swine models in conjunction with adipose-de-
rived stem cells (ADSCs) or ADSC-derived exosomes. If successful, this study will offer a translatable off-the-
shelf biomimetic NHC microporous plugs for PAF repair and tissue healing.

title: Next steps for PTSD genomics: from loci to function
text:
In the United States, approximately 8% of the civilian and up to 30% of the active military and veteran population
will experience post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), and, in the absence of diagnostic biomarkers and targeted
therapeutic interventions, the costs of PTSD are staggering. We will study the genomic architecture of PTSD,
with a focus on (i) gene expression, DNA methylation and protein expression of whole brain regions, (ii) gene
expression and epigenetics in individual brain cells, and (iii) SNP-specific CRIPSR-editing of iPSC derived cul-
tures exposed to glucocorticoids. Finally, we will characterize phenotypes associated with identified variants and
networks to better understand how molecular mechanisms underlying PTSD are linked to specific symptoms, to
improve PTSD prevention and treatment long-term.

title: MULTICOMPONENT MECHANOCHEMICAL REGULATION OF ACTIN FILAMENT END DYNAMICS
text:
Our research will advance our fundamental understanding of how cells control their shape and movement—
processes critical for wound healing, immune responses, and preventing metastatic cancer spread. By revealing
how mechanical forces and protein interactions regulate the actin cytoskeleton, our work could lead to new
therapies for neurodegenerative diseases, developmental disorders, and autoimmune conditions. These insights
may also inform treatments for pathological conditions involving aberrant cell migration, including fibrosis and
chronic inflammatory diseases.

title: Static and Dynamic Neurocircuitry Associated with Fluctuations in Non-Suicidal Self-Injury
text:
Non-suicidal self-injury (NSSI) commonly begins in adolescence and is associated with lifetime psychopathology
and increased risk for suicide; thus, there is a pressing need to better understand the processes of NSSI for the
advancement of more effective interventions. The proposed study will collect ecological momentary assessment
data at five timepoints spaced two months apart and also neuroimaging and clinical data from adolescents with
NSSI at three timepoints spaced 4 months apart, allowing for investigating both static (trait) and dynamic (state)
neurobiological features associated with this behavior. The proposed study will help disentangle static and
dynamic fluctuations associated with longitudinal variability in NSSI, yielding novel insights into NSSI-related
biobehavioral mechanisms, which could be targeted clinically.

title: Determining the roles of giant Starship transposons in horizontal gene transfer and fungal biology
text:
Starships are a newly discovered group of transposons that horizontally transfer genetic information within and
between species of fungal microbes. The proposed research program will develop new model systems to
determine the molecular mechanisms of horizontal Starship transfer and will characterize their previously
unconsidered impacts on fungal biology and evolution. This work will provide a necessary foundation for future
efforts to leverage Starship biology and fungal horizontal gene transfer into conceptually innovative disease
mitigation and health management strategies.

title: Refining neurophysiological biomarkers of epilepsy using deep learning to guide pediatric epilepsy surgery
text:
More than one-third of children with epilepsy do not respond to medications and are therefore candidates for
epilepsy surgery. Developing a robust tool to identify abnormal brain areas for surgical intervention would be a
groundbreaking advancement in treating children with epilepsy. This project aims to investigate promising spatial
neurophysiological biomarkers of the epileptic brain known as high-frequency oscillations through a novel deep
learning-based approach.

title: Core B: Proteomics and lipoprotein characterization core
text: The proteomics and lipoprotein characterization core (Core B) will provide the powerful tools of modern mass spectrometry and complex data set analysis to Program Project Grant (PPG) investigators. The Core will also provide lipoprotein isolation, and measurements of lipoprotein particle concentration and size using calibrated ion mobility analysis. The Core will permit structural identification and quantitation of lipoproteins including remnant lipoprotein particles (RLPs), as well as TRLs including IDL and VLDL, LDL and HDL, and measurement of lipoprotein particle number of these lipoprotein classes using calibrated ion mobility analysis. Core personnel are proficient in liquid chromatography-electrospray ionization-MS/MS analysis (shotgun proteomics) of complex biological mixtures of proteins, with a particular emphasis on the lipoprotein proteomes and on the quantification of their protein cargo using targeted LC-MSMS analysis. The Core Director established precise methods for quantitation of proteome of HDL and other lipoproteins, and applied them to quantification of the HDL proteome in large translational studies. He will apply the same methods to other lipoprotein classes through Core B. The Core personnel also have developed methods for kinetics of apolipoprotein in plasma and isolated lipoproteins, a methodology that will be used extensively by all PPG projects. The unique calibrated ion mobility analysis method measures proatherogenic particles, including RLPs and small dense LDL, in addition to HDL subpopulations. We anticipate that all investigators will take advantage of these capabilities. In addition to providing instrumental capabilities and bioinformatics tools, Core B staff will provide consultation and collaboration on the application of mass spectrometry and lipoprotein particle concentration measurements to the Program Project, and integration and analysis of complex datasets. This will include development of new analytical methods targeted at achieving the research objectives of the Program’s investigators. Core B will optimize the efficiency and cost-effectiveness through which these services are provided to PPG investigators by providing a central laboratory. This avoids the need for individual PPG investigators to maintain the required instrumentation in their own laboratories, avoids the high cost of commercial mass spectrometric services, and will ensure consistency between analyses for different project sites (Seattle, St. Louis, and New York). By centralizing and standardizing procedures, Core B will provide a common set of analytical tools that will lead to a unified understanding of molecular mechanisms involved in the physiologic and pathophysiologic processes of diabetic vascular disease.

title: Semantics Standards and Tools for Spatial and Contextual Exposome Data
text: To comprehensively understand the causes of diseases and prevent them, environmental exposures, especially the spatial and contextual exposome—contexts in which the person lives their life or external agents to which the one is exposed (e.g., environmental pollutants), need to be systematically explored. There is also an increasing interest in spatiotemporally linking spatial and contextual exposome data to real-world observational data including electronic health records (EHRs) and administrative claims data, to answer various questions on how exposures to environmental factors affect health status, disease development, and outcomes. Responding to RFA-ES-23-002, the objective of this proposal is to develop an innovative SPATIAL AND CONTEXTUAL EXPOSOME SEMANTIC DATA INTEGRATION SYSTEM (SPACESCANS) with (1) an ontology-annotated knowledge graph of existing publicly available high-quality spatial and contextual exposome data from heterogeneous sources, along with (2) a user-friendly data integration tool.

title: Epigenomic Mechanisms & STAT Networks in Persistent CA Candidemia
text:
This research is highly relevant to public health because hematogenously disseminated candidiasis is a frequent
hospital acquired infection that results in a high degree of mortality in adults and neonates, even with currently
available treatment. Discovering C. albicans and host immune signatures associated with lethality and
persistence during candidemia holds promise to provide new insight into the pathogenesis of disseminated
candidiasis. Furthermore, this information may be used to develop new diagnostic or therapeutic strategies
against this frequently fatal disease.

title: Epigenetic Regulation of Head and Neck Cancer Immune Evasion
text:
Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) is a physically deforming and often fatal disease with limited
treatment options. NSD1, a histone methyltransferase involved in epigenetic regulation of gene expression, is
inactivated in ~15% of HNSCC. This project proposes to understand the mechanism by which NSD1 loss
promotes the development of HNSCC, with a specific focus on the role of NSD1 in tumor immune escape.

title: Improving Health in Rheumatic Diseases (ImHeaRD)
text: Project Summary – Methodologic Core Addressing racial disparities in rheumatic diseases as complex as systemic lupus erythematosus and systemic sclerosis requires interdisciplinary approaches that involve strong methodological components. The overarching objectives of the CCCR Methodologic Core are to enhance the quality of research conducted by investigators in the CCCR Research Community and to provide leadership on investigations relevant to minority health in rheumatic diseases. To achieve these objectives within the CCCR, the Methodologic Core has 4 aims: 1) provide quantitative guidance to the CCCR Research Community; 2) conduct research to develop novel biostatistics methods; 3) participate in educational development of clinical and translational investigators; and 4) serve as liaisons between the CCCR Research Community and other quantitative experts. The Core is comprised of four PhD faculty with expertise in biostatistics, bioinformatics, and epidemiology, all of whom have a strong track record of collaboration with rheumatologists, clinically-relevant methods development, and education. Through interactions with our CTSA program and other important resources, the Core will also be able to leverage additional expertise as needed. By achieving these aims through innovative techniques, the Methodologic Core will help continue to ensure that MUSC is a leading entity in rheumatologic research.

title: SARS-CoV-2 protease inhibitors for treating COVID-19
text:
The COVID-19 pandemic caused by the highly transmissible and pathogenic SARS-CoV-
2 virus has become a catastrophic public health crisis worldwide. There are no approved vaccines
or effective antiviral medications for COVID-19 treatment or prevention. The proposed studies are
directed toward the design and development of broad-spectrum anti-coronaviral drugs to treat
COVID-19.

title: Use of Tiered Genetic Sequencing and Specialty Referral for Identifying and Managing Rare Genetic Causes of Chronic Suppurative Respiratory Disease
text:
Chronic suppurative respiratory tract disease is typically characterized by persistent and recurrent ear, sinus
and bronchial infections and eventually bronchiectasis. Genetic causes include primary ciliary dyskinesia
associated with abnormal airway clearance and inborn errors of immunity which can have very similar clinical
presentations. The purpose of this application is to evaluate a stepwise process for identifying, diagnosing and
managing these genetic diseases which can lead to increased possibilities for precision treatments and
improved clinical outcomes.

title: Development of CD46 theranostics for imaging and treatment of multiple myeloma
text:
This proposal describes the development and implementation of theranostic PET imaging and radionuclide
therapy agents targeting CD46, an exciting new therapeutic target which is highly expressed in multiple
myeloma. We will optimize this strategy in preclinical models, developing co-treatment methods to maximize
sensitivity. A pilot translational study of the PET imaging agent will be used to detect CD46 expression in
patients with multiple myeloma, setting the stage for widespread clinical translation of these techniques.

title: B7-H3 Targeted Ultrasound Molecular Imaging System for Early Breast Cancer and Metastatic Detection
text:
Current approaches for the diagnosis of early breast cancer (i.e. mammograms) in particular in women with
dense breast tissue have major limitations leading to delayed or missed diagnoses as well as false positive
results. This research will develop a new ultrasound imaging platform that allows diagnosing breast cancer with
high sensitivity and specificity to enable rapid and effective detection of breast cancer at an early, still curable
stage. The widespread and easy availability of ultrasound system in the clinics further improve the applicability
this technique and save the lives of many patients through early diagnosis.

title: Endocannabinoid Targeting for Opioid Induced Respiratory Depression
text:
The US is facing an unprecedented loss of life resulting from opioid overuse and the associated respiratory
depression (OIRD). This project will investigate targeting the cannabinoid receptor 2 (CB2R) as a novel
therapeutic target to mitigate OIRD induced by three commonly used recreational and medicinal opioids -
fentanyl, oxycodone, and heroin. Successful completion of proposed experiments will 1) reveal the mechanistic
role of the endocannabinoid system within the brainstem in regulating breathing under normal and OIRD states
and 2) validate activation of the CB2R as a safe and clinically useful therapy for opioid use disorder (OUD).
